what_worked: Exceptional narrative discipline: every slide earns its place, limitations disclosed, recommendations grounded in specific numbers.
fix_next: B2B median $1,240 and B2C $304 don't match reference benchmarks; TLD median for .ai ($1,914 vs reference $25) needs verification against the frozen dataset.
verdict: Outstanding strategic storytelling with a few unverifiable numbers that need tightening.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: Stripe listed as 87% of revenue; reference says $13.5M/$15.6M = 86.7%, borderline acceptable. Slide 8: B2B median $1,240 and B2C median $304 do not match reference medians (reference gives median multiples of 2.35x/2.30x but not these absolute values; the claim '4x the revenue' overstates the reference ~2.35x median multiple). Slide 10: .ai median shown as $1,914 vs reference median of $25 (n=91); .com shown as $204 vs reference median $8. These are off by orders of magnitude—likely using mean or a filtered subset rather than median. Slide 6: Top-10 share 49.6% matches reference, but 'Top 1 = 18.2%' implies Stan is $2.84M which is ~18.2% of $15.6M—plausible. Title says '11 startups own half' but top-10 is 49.6%, so 11 for 50% is reasonable.

evidence.insight: Slide 7 juxtaposes category crowding against median revenue to surface a non-obvious finding (AI crowded but low-paying vs Education). Slide 8's 'AI is a layer, not a market' reframes category data into strategic advice. Slide 11 introduces micro-acquisition as a curriculum pillar—genuinely original. Slide 9 quantifies the India monetisation gap as a market opportunity.
evidence.narrative: Clear thesis on slide 1 ('scaling is the bottleneck'), built through revenue reality (5), concentration (6), category (7), positioning (8), geography (9), distribution (10), marketplace (11), and synthesized into six recommendations (12). Every slide has an 'Insight for Praxel' that ties back to the thesis. The arc moves from problem → evidence → solution with no detours.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 states the ask explicitly. Slide 4 discloses limitations (self-selected sample, frozen snapshot, 216 zero-revenue rows). Each slide has a 'Not used' footnote explaining excluded data and why. Audience (Praxel course designers) is clear throughout. Scope is well-bounded.
evidence.accuracy: Slide 5: 579 under $1k and 58% checks out (579/1000). Median $400 is plausible but not directly verifiable. Mean $15,596 matches reference total/1000. Slide 6: Top-10 at 49.6% matches reference. Slide 7: AI median ~$503 and Education ~$2,435 match reference. Slide 10: TLD medians (.ai $1,914, .com $204) are dramatically higher than reference (.ai median $25, .com median $8)—this is a material error, likely confusing mean with median or using a filtered subset. Slide 8: B2B/B2C figures don't align with reference median multiples.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark/light theme alternation creates rhythm. Slide 5 bar chart is well-labeled with count annotations. Slide 7 dual-axis chart is appropriate and readable. Typography hierarchy is strong throughout—big numbers, supporting text, footnotes. No decorative graphics. Color is used sparingly and purposefully (orange for emphasis). Slide 8 splits into two clean panels.
evidence.ai_slop: none—the 'Not used' footnotes, specific limitation disclosures, and correlation caveats (slide 10 footer) demonstrate genuine analytical judgment rather than template filling. No generic filler language detected.
